data.title: Robinhood Stock (HOOD) Drops 4% as Two Employees Charged with Fraud
data.description:
The stock of online brokerage Robinhood Markets (HOOD) is down 4% after the U.S. Attorney's Office for New York charged two of the company's employees with fraud. Robinhood engineers Hefu Chai and Huaisong Xiang were each charged with commodities fraud and wire fraud arising from a scheme to misappropriate confidential business information from the company.

The stolen information was allegedly used to trade perpetual futures on the decentralized derivatives exchange called "Hyperliquid." According to the complaint filed in Manhattan federal court, Chai and Xiang had access to nonpublic information related to whether and when Robinhood will support additional cryptocurrencies for trading.

The two used that information to make profitable bets on Hyperliquid, according to the lawsuit.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Gains With Multiple Defense Contracts
data.description:
Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) is on a roll. It has landed multiple defense contracts that should represent stable income and help give the commercial aircraft space room to breathe. This was welcome news for investors as well, who gave Boeing shares a fractional boost in Tuesday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 2.21% loss in its share price over the past year.

New Ceiling, Old Contract

One of the biggest wins in defense contracts for Boeing came from the KC-46 contract between Boeing and the United States Air Force. That contract already existed, but it was modified to have a new maximum value: up to $19.1 billion, which allows for increased foreign sales.

This meant an additional $13.4 billion in value was added to the contract from its original amount. With the new contract, Boeing can sell to Japan, Israel, and other countries that have yet to be named, "future partners," noted a report from Investor's Business Daily.

Production Contract Kicks In

Boeing also set up a new contract with the United States Navy. The contract, a $562 million fixed-price incentive contract, is sufficient to start off Lot 1 Low Rate Initial Production on the MQ-25A Stingray, according to a report from Navy Times.

With this, the Navy will have access to an unmanned tanker system, the first of its kind for the navy so far. It also serves as the Navy's first operational unmanned aircraft that works from a carrier. With this tool in place, the Navy can continue using its F/A-18 Super Hornet aircraft, and keep fighter jets from being used as air-to-air refueling systems.

data.title: Rivian vs. Lucid: One EV Stock Looks More Like the Next Tesla, Says Investor
data.description:
Tesla's rise from a niche electric car maker to a company worth more than $1 trillion offers an important lesson for investors hunting for the next big EV winner. Elon Musk's original strategy was straightforward: start with an expensive, desirable vehicle, use the cash and experience gained to move into cheaper models, and eventually reach a mass-market audience.

That strategy took years to play out, but it gave Tesla the manufacturing scale, cash generation and brand recognition needed to pursue bigger opportunities such as autonomous driving and robotaxis.

Following in Tesla's wake, both Rivian (NASDAQ:RIVN) and Lucid (NASDAQ:LCID) are trying to establish themselves as major EV players, but they are taking rather different routes. And with Rivian valued at roughly $23 billion vs. ~$1.60 billion for Lucid, the two stocks offer very different risk-reward profiles.

Investor Ryan Vanzo, who contributes to The Motley Fool, believes that for those looking for a potential Tesla successor, one of them is a far more likely candidate to give the EV leader a run for its money.

The difference between the way these companies are going about their business is particularly clear when looking at the latest vehicle launches. Lucid's Gravity SUV is positioned firmly at the luxury end of the market, with a starting price of almost $126,000. Once options, taxes and other costs are included, buyers could easily be looking at more than $150,000.

That may help Lucid build a premium brand, but it does little to solve one of the biggest challenges facing an EV startup: achieving the volume necessary to build a sustainable business.

Rivian's strategy looks very different. Its R2 SUV starts at roughly $45,000, with more expensive versions reaching around $60,000. That puts the vehicle much closer to the price range of mainstream consumers. Rivian also plans to follow the R2 with the cheaper R3 and R3X, giving it a potential path toward much greater production volumes.

Vanzo argues that this puts Rivian closer to the playbook Tesla used to build its business. Lucid has lower-priced vehicles in development too, but its planned mass-market model has already been pushed back from 2026 to late 2027, raising questions about how quickly it can expand beyond the luxury market.

The same advantage might extend to autonomous driving and robotaxis. Both companies are developing self-driving technology, but Rivian's much larger market value gives it considerably more financial firepower. Vanzo notes that Rivian could raise an amount greater than Lucid's entire market cap through only a relatively small amount of shareholder dilution.

There is also evidence that outside companies see value in Rivian's manufacturing ambitions. Uber has agreed to purchase as many as 50,000 R2 vehicles as it builds out its robotaxi plans. Its separate agreement with Lucid covers 35,000 vehicles.

That does not guarantee Rivian will succeed, and Uber is clearly spreading its bets. Still, Vanzo sees the larger commitment to Rivian as another indication that the company is better positioned to supply vehicles at scale while developing the software needed for autonomous driving.

For investors willing to accept the risks of an unprofitable EV maker, Vanzo therefore sees Rivian as the more compelling choice. "Despite a higher valuation, Rivian shares look more attractive given the company's larger manufacturing scale, low-cost model launches, and a seemingly more advanced self-driving tech platform," the investor summed up. (To watch Vanzo's track record, click here)

The Street, however, does not seem to be enamored with either EV maker, as both claim Hold consensus ratings. RIVN shares are expected to appreciate by 8% over the coming year, considering the average price target clocks in at $17.06. Interestingly, assisted by a highly bullish call, LCID's $8.71 average target points to 12-month returns of 115%. (See RIVN stock forecast or LCID stock forecast)

data.title: General Motors Stock (GM) Falls as Automaker Warns of Weak Sales
data.description:
General Motors' (GM) stock is down 2% after the Detroit automaker warned that its sales are likely to be weaker than expected in the fourth and final quarter of this year. Speaking at an investment conference, General Motors' Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Paul Jacobson said that the company expects sales in the fourth quarter to be "seasonally weaker" than in the the second and third quarters of the year.

Jacobson said that the final months of 2026 are likely to be challenging due to 35,000 fewer of the automaker's trucks being delivered this autumn as expected. He added that 2027 is "going to be a bit of a flat spot" for electric vehicle sales at GM. However, the CFO stressed that the final quarter of the year is usually "seasonally weaker" than the spring and summer months, when vehicle sales tend to be strongest.

General Motors' Electric Vehicles

"EV profitability has been hit really hard over the last couple of years. First, tariffs; second, everybody was logging EV credits as part of the variable profit equation…both of those went the wrong direction against profitability," said Jacobson at the conference. GM still believes that electric vehicles are a long-term play, "but we've got to get them profitable," added Jacobson.

data.title: Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Slips as It Patches Patches
data.description:
Remember when tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) issued that massive patch last week? The one that patched up nearly 1,000 separate flaws in one day, many of which were found with the aid of artificial intelligence (AI)? Well, it turns out that that massive patch needed a patch of its own, as Microsoft is rolling out an emergency update to the patch to fix issues with it. That did not sit well with investors, and Microsoft shares slipped fractionally in Tuesday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 0.71% loss in its share price over the past year.

Patching Patches

A report from The Verge noted that the massive patch that fixed nearly a thousand issues by itself came with a few new bugs that no one expected. Several issues emerged, and showed up in a surprisingly wide range of products. Virtual machines running Hyper-V were impacted, as were Remote Desktop Services users and even some audio devices that ran on USB connections.

Normally, Microsoft does not issue out-of-band updates for Windows. But in recent months, such updates are proving necessary. Back in January, Microsoft had to roll out four such updates following a Windows 11 patch that proved buggier than expected,and two emergency updates came out in March after an update rendered some unable to sign into Microsoft accounts.

Priced Out of Gaming

Game subscriptions are welcome for the companies who release them. Instead of just selling a game and being done with it, the customers end up paying for the same game over and over again over a period of months, even years. But a changing economic picture is shaking up the concept of subscription services for games, with over 40% of people canceling such services citing costs as the main reason.

The word from Games Industry says that costs are "…becoming a stronger driver of US cancellations" across Xbox Game Pass Essential, as well as its competitors' services. This does not necessarily mean that more people are canceling. Rather, when they do cancel, cost is an increasingly primary driver. Microsoft responded to such conditions back in April, cutting Game Pass' highest-end price, but all the major firms in this market have hiked prices on hardware.

data.title: Micron Stock (MU) Up on New 512GB DDR5 Module Reveal for AI Data Centers
data.description:
Micron (MU) stock was up 0.08% Tuesday after the semiconductor memory and storage solutions company announced a new product to appeal to AI data center operators. The company has shown off what it calls the world's first 512GB DDR5 memory module. The new module is aimed at data centers running AI, data analysis, in-memory databases, and other large workloads.

The 512GB module uses Micron's vertical packaging tech to stack DRAM dies and link them with through-silicon vias. That design packs more memory into each DRAM package without giving up the speed needed in current data center systems. A 24-slot, dual-socket server can hold up to 12TB of DDR5 DRAM. Micron also said the new module can cut power use by more than 60% versus using four 128GB DDR5 modules.

Micron noted that the memory is built for the rising load that comes with AI data. It also pointed out that for some data jobs, the 512GB modules can deliver up to 1.4 times the speed of 256GB DDR5 setups. The modules can also help memory-heavy tools such as RocksDB and Redis handle more data and more users. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Intel (INTC) are working with Micron to test the modules across next-gen server platforms.

Micron expects volume output of the 512GB RDIMM in the second half of 2027, based on customer needs.
